advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In `_check_marker`, only honor a preceding-line marker when that line is a standalone comment (stripped line starts with `#`), so an inline marker on the prior field's definition is not misattributed to the next field.
evidence: scripts/check_config_reads.py:72-81: `candidates = [lineno - 1] ... candidates.append(lineno - 2) ... m = _MARKER_RE.search(lines[idx]); if m: return True, m.group(1).strip()`

Real adjacency exists: `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:396: lock_lease_secs: int = 120  # read-via: ...` is immediately followed by `:397: deletion_probe_limit: int = 20` (unmarked). Checking line 397: own line has no marker, preceding line 396 matches `_MARKER_RE`, so 397 is falsely credited with lock_lease_secs's marker.

Masked in the real tree only because `deletion_probe_limit` has a genuine read at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:583: _budget = load_config().reconciler.deletion_probe_limit`; the reads-path passes it before the marker path, so the bug is latent, not observed.
advisory.finding: `_check_marker` credits a field with a `# read-via:` marker found on the immediately PRECEDING source line without requiring that line to be a standalone comment. When an inline-marked field is directly followed by an unmarked, genuinely-dead field, the dead field's preceding-line lookback matches the prior field's inline marker and is silently treated as justified — a false negative that lets a truly inert field pass the gate.
scenarios: A future dead field added immediately below any inline-`# read-via:`-marked field (the schema has several: lines 221, 222, 396) would silently pass the gate.
advisory.suggested_fix: When considering the preceding line (`lineno - 2`), require `lines[idx].lstrip().startswith('#')` before accepting the marker; keep the own-line (`lineno - 1`) check accepting inline markers.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a held-out test: field A with an inline `# read-via:` marker immediately followed by field B with no marker and no read site — assert the gate reports field B.
evidence: `test_marker_on_the_preceding_line_is_honoured` (lines 83-89) only exercises a STANDALONE comment on the preceding line, never an inline-marked field followed by a dead field.

No test constructs two adjacent fields where field A carries an inline `# read-via:` and field B is unmarked+unread; `test_every_dead_field_is_reported_not_just_the_first` (lines 100-110) uses two unmarked fields, not this adjacency.
advisory.finding: The held-out edge suite does not cover the inline-marked-field-immediately-followed-by-unmarked-dead-field case, so the preceding-line marker misattribution defect passes CI undetected.
scenarios: The misattribution regression could ship because no test asserts a dead field following an inline-marked field still fires.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the marker regex to a comment that is (or begins with) the marker token rather than matching `read-via:` anywhere in the line.
evidence: scripts/check_config_reads.py:24: `_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"#\s*read-via:(.*)")` uses `.search`, so any occurrence of `read-via:` in the comment text (e.g. `# NOTE: the read-via: convention is documented elsewhere`) matches and returns a non-empty pointer.
advisory.finding: `_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"#\s*read-via:(.*)")` matches the token anywhere inside a comment, so a descriptive/prose comment that merely mentions `read-via:` on the field line or preceding line would be misread as a valid marker and suppress a legitimate firing.
scenarios: A comment discussing the marker convention near a dead field would silently satisfy the gate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a held-out case asserting `check` collects/gates fields on `@dataclass()`, `@dataclasses.dataclass`, and `@dataclasses.dataclass()`-decorated schema classes.
evidence: Test fixtures use only bare `@dataclass`: `_SCHEMA_ONE_FIELD` and `_SCHEMA` both start `@dataclass\nclass ...`
search 'dataclasses.dataclass' in tests/scripts → no matches; the dotted/call decorator branches are untested
ABSENCE: no test constructs a schema decorated with `@dataclass()` or `@dataclasses.dataclass[()]`, so a field-collection regression on those forms is undetectable
advisory.finding: The three non-bare `@dataclass` decorator forms handled by `_is_dataclass` (`@dataclass()`, `@dataclasses.dataclass`, `@dataclasses.dataclass()`) are never exercised: every test fixture (`_SCHEMA_ONE_FIELD`, `_SCHEMA`) and the real schema use only the bare `@dataclass`. A regression that mis-handles the `ast.Call`/`ast.Attribute` branches (dropping field collection for a `@dataclass()`- or `@dataclasses.dataclass`-decorated section) would pass the entire suite while silently exempting those fields from the gate.
scenarios: A section dataclass declared as `@dataclass(frozen=True)` or `@dataclasses.dataclass` would have its fields silently un-gated if `_is_dataclass` regressed on the Call/Attribute branches
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized held-out test that varies the decorator form (`@dataclass`, `@dataclass()`, `@dataclasses.dataclass`, `@dataclasses.dataclass()`) over a zero-read field and asserts each still produces exactly one error for the dead field.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where an unparseable `.py` in the scanned root holds a field's only read site and assert the documented behavior (currently: field reported as dead).
evidence: scripts/check_config_reads.py:91-94: `try: tree = ast.parse(...) except SyntaxError: continue`
ABSENCE: no test places an unparseable `.py` under the scanned root, so the skip path (and its false-failure consequence when the only read site is in that file) is unverified
advisory.finding: `_collect_reads` silently swallows `SyntaxError` for any scanned `.py` file (`except SyntaxError: continue`), but no test exercises this path. A malformed module in the source tree is skipped, so a read site inside it is dropped — which can turn a genuinely-read field into a FALSE gate failure. The swallow behavior is untested in either direction.
scenarios: A source file with a syntax error that contains the sole read site of a field causes the gate to false-fail on that field, undetected by tests
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a held-out test writing a syntactically invalid `.py` containing `return o.ghost_knob` and assert `check` still reports `ghost_knob` (documenting the fail-quiet skip), pinning the intended behavior.
